validity.recommendation: No change — existence, classification, and duplicate status all confirmed. Keep as a distinct row from P2289.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/DUPLICATE/CLASSIFICATION checked first per priority order. gazeta.uz (2023-02-27, Russian, independent of GEM) states the Bukhara-Ural system has TWO existing lines: Line 1 'Gazli-Chelyabinsk', launched 1963, and Line 2 'Gazli-Chelyabinsk-Sverdlovsk', launched 1966 — before describing a planned third line (construction started near Aktobe 2023). This is a clean, independent match to the roster split: P2289 (Gazli->Chelyabinsk Oblast) = Line I; P5695 (Gazli->Sverdlovsk Oblast, this row) = Line II. GEM's StartYear1=1966 for P5695 matches the Line-2 launch year exactly. A second independent primary document, the December 2020 EIA 'Пояснительная записка' for the new KS-14-Aktobe branch (ecoportal.kz, hosted for a Kazakh public hearing, verified 200 via url_verifier and content-read with pdftotext) separately refers to '1 и 2 нитки МГ «Бухара-Урал»' (lines 1 and 2 of the Bukhara-Ural trunk) as two distinct physical pipes tied in at km 1387 of the corridor — independent primary confirmation that two genuine parallel strings exist, not a database double-count. So P5695 is NOT a duplicate of P2289: 'Bukhara-Ural genuinely is two parallel strings' per the orchestrator's lead is confirmed. Classification (transmission trunk gas pipeline, Fuel=Gas) is correct and uncontested by every source read (Russian 'магистральный газопровод' = trunk/transmission gas pipeline in all of gazeta.uz, ecoportal.kz, and KMG's own annual-report table headers 'TRUNK GAS PIPELINE — BUKHARA-URAL'). Two further concerns (length, capacity, ownership) are filed as separate validity entries below — this entry covers existence/duplicate/classification only, all clean.

validity.recommendation: Flag LengthKnown=2382.00 km as suspect — likely a mis-applied whole-system total, not Line II's own length. Route to Update to search for a genuine per-string length; no independent source located gives a per-line length breakdown for the full Gazli-Sverdlovsk route.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's LengthKnown for P5695 is 2,382.00 km. This is EXACTLY, to the decimal km, the figure KazMunayGas reports for 'Bukhara-Ural' as a SYSTEM TOTAL (both lines combined) in its Annual Report 2019 and Annual Report 2020 gas-transportation tables (verified 200, pdftotext-read: 'Bukhara-Ural ... 2,382 ... 31.5' in both ar2019 and ar2020 English-language strategic-report PDFs). KMG's table lists ONE row per named trunk system, not per string, so 2,382 km is the combined length of Line I + Line II together, not either line alone. A single-string row (P5695 = Line II only) carrying the identical whole-system figure is the same defect shape as the KMG-total-stamped-on-a-single-string pattern flagged elsewhere in this sweep (cf. P2291/P5770/P5771 capacity note) — strong circumstantial evidence the length was copied from the KMG aggregate rather than measured per string. Compounding this: P2289 (Line I, same corridor) carries a DIFFERENT total, 2,200 km, which is inconsistent with two genuinely parallel lines sharing one corridor (they should track closely, not differ by ~180 km, if both are truly full end-to-end lengths) — unless the two lines diverge over meaningfully different distances, which no source confirms. I could not find any independent source that gives a per-line length for the Kazakh+Uzbek+Russian route as a whole. The one per-string breakdown I found is geographically partial: RPI's 2009 'Oil and Gas Industry of Turkmenistan' report (independently hosted PDF, s3.amazonaws.com/rgi-documents, verified 200, pdftotext-read) states the Bukhara-Ural trunk crosses Turkmenistan with 'two lines of 118 km length, pipe diameter 1,020 mm' — i.e. only the ~118 km Turkmen transit segment is broken out by line, and even there the two lines are reported as equal length (118 km each), not the ~180 km spread GEM shows for the full route. This is a material, unresolved spec disagreement — do not treat 2,382 km as verified for Line II alone.

validity.recommendation: Flag Capacity=21.00 bcm/y as unverified — no independent source corroborates this figure for either string, and every source that gives a number is materially lower or scoped differently. Route to Update.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records Capacity=21.00 bcm/y for P5695, and the SAME 21.00 value is also recorded for P2289 (the other Bukhara-Ural string) — i.e. 42.0 bcm/y combined if the two strings are summed. No independent source I found supports 21.0 bcm/y for a single string, or 42.0 bcm/y combined: (1) RPI's 2009 Turkmenistan report states 'The design capacity of the Bukhara-Ural gas pipeline is 15 bcm of gas per year' for the WHOLE system (both lines), with actual throughput far lower (3.5-7.5 bcm/y by section) — well under GEM's per-string 21.0. (2) GulfPub (Tier 2, one source, never authoritative alone) carries three 'Bukhara-Ural' entries (ref_ids 5647/16965/16970, evidently one entity digitized three times) at Capacity_mmcfd=1700 = ~17.6 bcm/y, again for what appears to be the whole named pipeline, not a single string — lower than GEM's 21.0 per string. (3) KMG's own annual reports give a SYSTEM total of 31.5 bcm/y (AR2019/AR2020) or 44.6 bcm/y (AR2021, a different, non-comparable vintage/scope per the standing vintage warning — the ~20-35% shrink between AR2020 and AR2021 for the same six Intergas lines is a scope redefinition, not a real capacity change, so AR2021's 44.6 cannot be treated as confirming GEM's 42.0 combined). None of the three lines of evidence agree with each other OR with GEM's 21.0-per-string figure, and none isolate a single-string capacity. This is a genuine, material spec disagreement that no available source resolves — leaving unfilled rather than citing a ref that doesn't actually support the value.

validity.recommendation: Re-examine Owner1='Gazprom PJSC' at 100% — likely wrong or at minimum an oversimplification for a pipeline whose Kazakh section is run by a Kazakh state entity. Route to Update to research segmented/country-split ownership.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM's Owner/Owners tab records Owner1='Gazprom PJSC' at 100% for P5695 (a pipeline whose row spans StartCountryOrArea=Uzbekistan to EndCountryOrArea=Russia, transiting Kazakhstan). Independent evidence contradicts sole/100% Gazprom ownership: intergas.kz's own 'About the company' page (verified 200) states that AO 'Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya' — a subsidiary that 'enters into the composition of AO National Company QazaqGaz' (Kazakhstan's state gas company) — received Government-decreed status as 'National Operator for trunk gas pipelines' in July 2018, and that its regional management units (UMG Aktobe, UMG Kostanay) are the ones operating 'MG Бухара-Урал' within Kazakhstan. Separately, GulfPub's (Tier 2) three 'Bukhara-Ural' records list THREE shareholders — 'Gazprom, KazMunayGas, Uzbekneftegaz' — not Gazprom alone, consistent with the well-known pattern for these Soviet-era trans-boundary trunklines (each country's national gas company holds/operates the section on its own territory, with Gazprom historically holding transit/operational rights over the whole corridor under Soviet-era and post-Soviet transit agreements). A single Owner1=Gazprom PJSC/100% for the entire cross-border asset, with no co-owners recorded, does not match either independent source. I could not find a source that gives a precise ownership percentage split by country, so I am not proposing a replacement value — only flagging the existing 100%-Gazprom attribution as unverified and probably incomplete.

fills.researcher_notes: Status is inferable, not literal (per url_verifier docstring: don't require the literal word 'operating' as a substring). gazeta.uz (Feb 2023) describes both existing lines as currently carrying gas at up to 170% of nameplate capacity in winter and cites plans to add a third line to relieve them — clear present-tense operating context. KMG's AR2020 (English, PDF, verified 200; pdftotext-confirmed table row 'Bukhara-Ural 2,382 31.5' under the live 'Intergas Central Asia' trunk-pipeline operating table) independently reports it as a currently operated asset in a corporate annual report. Two independent origins, both consistent with 'operating'.

Both sources describe Bukhara-Ural as a 'газопровод'/'gas pipeline' carrying natural gas (ecoportal.kz EIA doc gives internal diameter/pressure specs for the natural-gas trunk; KMG's report is titled 'Gas Transportation' and lists Bukhara-Ural under gas trunk pipelines). Content confirmed by manual pdftotext read — url_verifier's substring screen fails on Cyrillic/large-PDF extraction (documented false-negative in its docstring), not on actual support.

ecoportal.kz's EIA repeatedly calls the line 'МГ «Бухара-Урал»' (магистральный газопровод = trunk/transmission gas pipeline). KMG's AR2020 table header explicitly labels it 'TRUNK GAS PIPELINE — BUKHARA-URAL'. Both independently confirm transmission-trunk classification, matching GEM.

gazeta.uz states explicitly: Line 2 ('Gazli-Chelyabinsk-Sverdlovsk', matching P5695's route) was launched in 1966. RPI's 2009 Turkmenistan report (pdftotext-confirmed) independently states 'In November 1966 ... gas was first transported ... through the Bukhara-Urals gas pipeline' following the Feb-1966 discovery of the Odzhak field — an independent primary/industry source anchoring 1966 as a real, meaningful start date for this pipeline's gas flow, consistent with (though not itself line-specific to) GEM's StartYear1=1966 for Line II.

ecoportal.kz's Dec-2020 EIA gives, for the shared corridor: '1 и 2 нитки МГ «Бухара-Урал»: ... Внутренний диаметр газопровода: 1000 мм' — internal diameter 1000mm for BOTH existing lines (pdftotext-confirmed, page ~34 of the PDF). RPI's independent 2009 Turkmenistan report gives the Turkmenistan-transit portion of Bukhara-Ural (2 lines) as pipe diameter 1,020mm. The two figures are complementary, not conflicting — 1000mm nominal/internal bore corresponds to a ~1020mm outer-diameter pipe under standard Russian/Soviet GOST steel-pipe sizing — and together they independently corroborate GEM's exact dual value '1000, 1020' mm.

gazeta.uz names Line 2 explicitly as 'Gazli-Chelyabinsk-Sverdlovsk' — Gazli (Uzbekistan's giant gas field/town near Bukhara) is the named origin point. Single strong source (no second independent source named 'Gazli' specifically for this line — KMG's reports mention Gazli only in the separate 'Gazli-Shymkent' pipeline's name, and GulfPub's matching records give 'Bukhara' rather than 'Gazli' as start_loc), so tier=medium rather than high.

gazeta.uz names Line 2's full route as 'Gazli-Chelyabinsk-Sverdlovsk', matching GEM's Gazli (Uzbekistan) -> Yekaterinburg/Sverdlovsk Oblast (Russia) end-to-end. Only one independent source gives this specific end-to-end route for Line II by name (GulfPub's matching records instead end at Chelyabinsk, more consistent with Line I or an aggregated/simplified digitization) — tier=medium, single strong source, not corroborated by a second independent naming of Sverdlovsk as the terminus.

summary: P5695 (Bukhara-Ural Line II, Gazli->Sverdlovsk) is confirmed real, correctly classified, and NOT a duplicate of P2289 (Line I, Gazli->Chelyabinsk) — gazeta.uz independently names both lines with 1963/1966 launch years matching the roster split exactly, and refs added for Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Start/Diameter/FuelSource/Location (mostly high tier). Three unresolved spec/attribution concerns: LengthKnown=2,382 km exactly matches KMG's SYSTEM-WIDE total (both lines combined), not a per-string figure; Capacity=21.00 bcm/y (also on P2289, i.e. 42 combined) disagrees with every independent source (RPI 15 bcm/y system design, GulfPub ~17.6, KMG system total 31.5/44.6 depending on vintage); and Owner1=Gazprom PJSC/100% conflicts with intergas.kz (Kazakh section run by QazaqGaz's Intergas Central Asia, National Operator since 2018) and GulfPub (3-way ownership). No fills for Length/Capacity/Owner — left UNRESOLVED rather than citing a ref that doesn't actually support the recorded value.
